{{Recipe summary|category=Bread recipes|servings=6|time=prep: 10 minutes
resting: 30 minutes
cooking: ~5 minutes|difficulty=2|energy=250 Cal each (if cooked in oil, 700 Cal each)}} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Native American cuisine|Native American Cuisine]] '''Fry bread''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Native American cuisine|Native American]] [[cookbook:flatbread|flatbread]] usually made on an open fire or a [[Cookbook:Barbecue|barbecue]], or fried in a pan of hot oil over a stove top. This recipe uses modern techniques and tools. Fry bread is best served hot, topped with melted margarine, [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] or [[Cookbook:Agave Syrup|agave nectar]], berry [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]], or [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] and [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]. ==Ingredients== * 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] * 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]] * ⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] hot water ==Procedure== # Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. # Use a [[Cookbook:Pastry Blender|pastry blender]] (or two butter knives) to cut the shortening into the flour. # Add the hot water, and mix until the water is incorporated and you get a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. # Turn out the dough on a lightly floured board. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough until it is soft and smooth. # Wrap the dough in [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic]], and let the dough rest for 30 minutes. # Divide the dough into 6 pieces, roll each into a ball, and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll]] each into a flat disk with a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]]. # [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] one side of each disk with melted margarine and place on a barbecue over a 3 Mississippi fire. # Brush the opposing side of the bread with margarine and flip the bread on the barbecue. # Cook until both sides are golden brown. Serve hot. == Notes, tips, and variations == * You can substitute either ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] plain [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]], or a ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] soured milk as a leavening agent instead of baking powder. If you do, add 2 hours to the rest time for the dough, and leave the dough somewhere warm. You can optionally include the baking powder as well to get a very puffy version of frybread. If using yogurt or soured milk for leavening, use ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] instead of ⅓ cup water. * You can use [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]] in place of shortening for a crispy, crunchier texture. * You can also [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the dough in hot oil over a [[Cookbook:Stovetop|stovetop]]. The dough cooks rapidly and will brown in about 12 seconds and must be turned over to allow the opposite side to brown, then be removed from the oil and placed sideways into a colander or large bowl lined with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]] to allow the oil to drain off the finished product [[Category:Recipes for flatbread]] [[Category:Grilled recipes]] [[Category:Vegan recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Native American recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes using baking powder]] [[Category:Recipes using wheat flour]]

steps.text: Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Use a pastry blender (or two butter knives) to cut the shortening into the flour.
Add the hot water, and mix until the water is incorporated and you get a dough.
Turn out the dough on a lightly floured board. Knead the dough until it is soft and smooth.
Wrap the dough in plastic, and let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces, roll each into a ball, and roll each into a flat disk with a rolling pin.
Brush one side of each disk with melted margarine and place on a barbecue over a 3 Mississippi fire.
Brush the opposing side of the bread with margarine and flip the bread on the barbecue.
Cook until both sides are golden brown. Serve hot.
